case_title: Gurmail Singh v. State of Punjab
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.34; Arms Act s.27
aggravating_circumstances: Common intention, enmity between parties, use of weapons, fatal injury
trial_court_outcome: Conviction of Gurnam Singh, Gurmail Singh, Gurcharan Singh and Sher Singh; acquittal of Avtar Singh, Dharam Pal Singh, Nachhattar Singh and Parshottam Singh
neutral_facts: The accused, who were all from the same family, had a dispute with the victim's family due to the victim's son teasing the daughter of one of the accused. The accused gathered in a house, consumed liquor, and then came out into the street with weapons, raising a lalkara (threatening retribution). They attacked the victim and his brother, causing injuries. The victim's brother succumbed to his injuries. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts and medical evidence, including a post-mortem report. The accused claimed the dispute arose from election rivalries and some had alibis. The trial court acquitted some accused and convicted others for the murder of the victim's brother. The High Court affirmed the trial court's decision.
